# WoW API: CreateFrame

From AddOn Studio

Jump to navigation Jump to search

## Contents

    + 1\.1 Arguments
    + 1\.2 Returns
* 2 Example

← WoW API < CreateFrame

Creates a new UI frame .

```
newFrame = CreateFrame("frameType"[, "frameName"[, parentFrame[, "inheritsFrame"]]]);
```

## Parameters

### Arguments

    frameType
String - Type of the frame to be created (XML tag name): "Frame", "Button", etc. See UIOBJECT\_Frame
frameName
    String - Name of the newly created frame. If nil, no frame name is assigned. The function will also set a global variable of this name to point to the newly created frame.
parentFrame
    Frame - The frame object that will be used as the created Frame's parent (cannot be a string!) Does not default to UIParent if given nil.
inheritsFrame
    String - a comma-delimited list of names of virtual frames to inherit from (the same as in XML). If nil, no frames will be inherited. These frames cannot be frames that were created using this function, they must be created using XML with **virtual="true"** in the tag.

### Returns

    newFrame
    Frame - Reference to the newly created frame.

## Example

Result: displays the horde and alliance insignias in the middle of the screen.

```
local f = CreateFrame("Frame",nil,UIParent)
f:SetFrameStrata("BACKGROUND")
f:SetWidth(128) -- Set these to whatever height/width is needed 
f:SetHeight(64) -- for your Texture

local t = f:CreateTexture(nil,"BACKGROUND")
t:SetTexture("Interface\\Glues\\CharacterCreate\\UI-CharacterCreate-Factions.blp")
t:SetAllPoints(f)
f.texture = t

f:SetPoint("CENTER",0,0)
f:Show()
```

## Notes

* CreateFrame() was added in 1.10
* The fourth argument, inheritFrame, was added in 1.11
* Frames CANNOT be deleted. Reuse them.
* The frame's OnLoad handler , which will only exist if inherited, will be executed during the CreateFrame call. Any OnLoad script handlers set after CreateFrame() will not execute; consider adding any non-inherited OnLoad code directly after a CreateFrame call or use XML frames instead.
* The returned frame reference is not strictly necessary because you can access frames by their global name if you give them one.
For performance reasons, however, it is advised to store frame references in local variables and use those instead of getting frames by their global name.
* See also API\_Frame\_SetScript to handle OnFunction scripts when not using a template.
* The most common uses for this function are:
  
    + Creating anonymous event handlers") .
    + Creating anonymous script handlers .
    + Creating frames on the fly for occasions when you don't know how many frames will be needed.
    + Creating infrequently used frames "on demand", for example: config dialogs, raid frames.
* Never forget to unset the frames parent, if you want to get rid of a frame. I would suggest to hide the frame via frame: Hide () and to use frame: [SetParent](https://addonstudio.org/mw1/index.php?title=WoW:API_Region_SetParent&action=edit&redlink=1 "WoW:API Region SetParent (page does not exist)") (nil) afterward (this will remove the frame from its parents child list).
If you just hide the frame without this additional step, frames created afterward will get a higher [framelevel](https://addonstudio.org/mw1/index.php?title=WoW:FrameLevel&action=edit&redlink=1 "WoW:FrameLevel (page does not exist)") than the hidden one. After a while, you will get frames at maximum [framelevel](https://addonstudio.org/mw1/index.php?title=WoW:FrameLevel&action=edit&redlink=1 "WoW:FrameLevel (page does not exist)") which are likely to be drawn in a distorted way (false order caused by equal [framelevel](https://addonstudio.org/mw1/index.php?title=WoW:FrameLevel&action=edit&redlink=1 "WoW:FrameLevel (page does not exist)") ).

# BackdropTemplate issues

Guides UI and Macro

[jere-16097](https://us.forums.blizzard.com/en/wow/u/jere-16097) (jere) November 2, 2021, 9:57pm 1

A lot of my addons started tossing lua errors this patch and some may not be updated which means I may have to manually update them. One of the major issues seems to be coming from this change:

> SharedTooltipTemplate and GameTooltipTemplate no longer inherit BackdropTemplate
> 
> 

For example in Astral keys, the tooltip frame is currently created this way:

> local AstralKeyToolTip = CreateFrame( “GameTooltip”, “AstralKeyToolTip”, AAFrame, “GameTooltipTemplate” )
> 
> 

But as the note says that GameTooltipTemplate no longer inherits BackdropTemplate so all the backdrop functions are now failing. Is there an easy way for me to modify this to reintroduce the BackdropTemplate functionality.

Side note, the AAFrame (the parent class) in that call seems to come from out of nowhere.

...

Do you have the actual error and the line mentioned in it?

It’s unlikely that line in itself is causing an error.

[DahkCeles-375955](https://us.forums.blizzard.com/en/wow/u/DahkCeles-375955) (DahkCeles) November 3, 2021, 2:24am 9

The whole `BackdropTemplateMixin and "BackdropTemplate" or nil` was a way of writing code that was compatible for both classic and retail, when the backdrop rules were inconsistent between them all.

It’s no longer necessary. Anything that should be a backdrop can just simply inherit `"BackdropTemplate"` as the fourth argument in CreateFrame.

excerpts:
World of Warcraft Forums

# Showing Elements in Combat Lockdown

Guides UI and Macro

[Rylak-3034442](https://us.forums.blizzard.com/en/wow/u/Rylak-3034442) (Rylak) August 18, 2020, 3:30am 1

Hi everyone,

Taints have recently become a bit of an issue in my addon and I believe that the cause is showing/hiding UI addon-generated elements such as frames and buttons during combat.  
I understand that Show/HideUIPanel is now a protected function and cannot be used during combat lockdown as of 8.2.0, but could anyone please confirm if frame:Show() has the same restrictions?  
I assume that :Show() is called from within ShowUIPanel so I’m guessing that the answer would be yes.

How do you personally work around this combat restriction? I maintain a loot distribution addon so a lot of the time loot will be distributed while the rest of the raid continues to clear so combat lockdown will regularly be a concern.

[Gello-89115](https://us.forums.blizzard.

...

Once you start using secure frames you’re bound by its rules and you’ll start to get into arcana that may be overkill for what you’re after.

If you have a button that inherits SecureActionButtonTemplate and parent it to a very basic frame, that parent frame is now protected and its parent up the chain.

Here’s a pair of frames where the parent frame (Fr1) has a “Click Me” button that shows a child frame (Fr2) that contains a secure button (pet heal) the traditional way:

```
-- main frame is not protected yet
local f1 = Fr1 or CreateFrame("Frame", "Fr1", UIParent, "BasicFrameTemplate")
f1:SetSize(200,200)
f1:SetPoint("CENTER")

-- child of f1, so far unsecure too
local f2 = Fr2 or CreateFrame("Frame", "Fr2", Fr1, "BasicFrameTemplate")
f2:SetSize(200,200)
--f2:SetPoint("RIGHT",f1,"LEFT")
f2:SetPoint("CENTER",-300,0)
f2:Hide()

-- child of f1 too, "Click Me" button that shows f2
local b1 = Bt1 or CreateFrame("Button", "Bt1", Fr1, "UIPanelButtonTemplate")
b1:SetWidth(80)

...

`local b1 = Bt1 or CreateFrame(“Button”, “Bt1”, Fr1, “UIPanelButtonTemplate,SecureHandlerClickTemplate”)`  
and we’ll replace this:  
`b1:SetScript(“OnClick”,function(self) f2:Show() end)`  
with this:  
`b1:SetFrameRef(“Fr2”,Fr2)  
b1:SetAttribute(“_onclick”,[[ self:GetFrameRef(“Fr2”):Show() ]])`

b1 (the “Click Me” button) will show Fr2 from the secure environment. (There are various ways of doing this btw.)

```
-- main frame is not protected yet
local f1 = Fr1 or CreateFrame("Frame", "Fr1", UIParent, "BasicFrameTemplate")
f1:SetSize(200,200)
f1:SetPoint("CENTER")

-- child of f1, so far unsecure too
local f2 = Fr2 or CreateFrame("Frame", "Fr2", Fr1, "BasicFrameTemplate")
f2:SetSize(200,200)
f2:SetPoint("RIGHT",f1,"LEFT")
f2:Hide()

-- child of f1 too, "Click Me" button that shows f2
local b1 = Bt1 or CreateFrame("Button", "Bt1", Fr1, "UIPanelButtonTemplate,SecureHandlerClickTemplate")
b1:SetSize(80,24)
b1:SetPoint("CENTER")
b1:SetText("Click Me")
-- your new OnClick is a secure _click snippet, and it needs to know what it will show beforehand; here by creating a frame reference
b1:SetFrameRef("Fr2",Fr2)
b1:SetAttribute("_onclick",[[ self:GetFrameRef("Fr2"):Show() ]])

-- adding this button to heal battle pets to f2 now makes f2 protected, and ALSO f1. everything up the parent chain gets protected
local b2 = Bt2 or CreateFrame("ItemButton", "Bt2", Fr2, "SecureActionButtonTemplate")
b2:SetPoint("CENTER")
b2.icon:SetTexture(644389)
b2:SetAttribute("type","spell")
b2:SetAttribute("spell","Revive Battle Pets")

-- now the Click Me button will show Fr2 in combat
```

Now to show Fr1 you’ll need to use a secure method too, which can be a click key binding or a secure button bound to a key or other methods.

Recommended reading include the secure execution stuff on wowpedia:

[Wowpedia](https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Secure_Execution_and_Tainting)

### [Secure Execution and Tainting](https://wowpedia.fandom.
com/wiki/Secure_Execution_and_Tainting)

The User Interface API mandates human decision-making, particularly in combat, by protecting many functions from insecure or tainted use. This security model was largely introduced in Patch 2.0[1] and has been a cornerstone of the API ever since.

And of course the authoritave reference for the secure environment from Iriel:  
<http://www.iriel.org/wow/docs/SecureHeadersGuide-4.0-r1.pdf>

[Rylak-3034442](https://us.forums.blizzard.com/en/wow/u/Rylak-3034442) (Rylak) August 18, 2020, 12:01pm 5

To my knowledge, I’m not inheriting from any secure templates. The only templates any of my frames inherit from are:

* InputBoxTemplate
* GameMenuButtonTemplate
* UIOptionsCheckButtonTemplate
* UIPanelScrollFrameTemplate
* GameFontNormal
* GameFontNormalSmall
* GameFontNormalLarge
* UIOptionsCheckButtonTemplate

Having said that - when I first made the addon, I constructed a fully independent set of frames for the options menu.
Earlier this year, I changed my options implementation from a custom frame to using the stock interface options panel.  
I imagine that this would make all of the attached frames and their children protected, wouldn’t it?

Edit: So on that last note, is Show/HideUIPanel only considered a protected function on **protected** frames? The bulk of my addon is not attached to any other frame (unless by default everything is attached to UIParent?) and so do you think I can freely show/hide frames in my main frame, but just apply combat lockdown restrictions on the options interface?

[Gello-89115](https://us.forums.blizzard.com/en/wow/u/Gello-89115) (Gello) August 18, 2020, 1:51pm 6

It’s okay to use the InterfaceOptionsPanel but it’s a viper’s nest of taint waiting to happen unrelated to how you use it.
Unless you’ve modified the cancel button to be an okay button (I don’t have my regular WoW machine available so can’t look it up), just opening/closing options during combat can taint action bars even if you’ve only given it a blank frame that does nothing.

If you’re letting the options panel handle the showing/hiding of the frame you should not have to worry about protected elements within the frame; but you should probably avoid getting creative and having popouts parented to the frame and such.

I don’t have any advice on Hide/ShowUIPanel, sorry. I avoid it since I generally don’t do panel-like behavior so trivial stuff like SetShown can be done without it.
